elements.text: Reference cards — decoration markers, PreToolUse gate, code style, sub-agent roles, memory scopes, MCP/slash, test pyramid

label.text:
Decoration markers (v9 · round-3)

@intent <path> [<clause-ids>]
    declarations OR non-declaration statements
    focal claim — 'this is what makes
    the clause hold'

@intent-support <path> [<clause-ids>]
                [<subj>, <pred>, <obj>]
    non-declaration statements only
    inline NL triple describes statement role
    SLOTS ARE ALWAYS AFFIRMATIVE

@intent-test <path>/<configured-suffix>
    test declarations

@intent-test-file <path>/<configured-suffix>
    file-scope test claim · top of file

@intent-file / @intent-ignore  (unchanged)

— Polarity (NEW v9 round-3) —
Triples carry polarity: positive | negative
(default positive). Slots stay affirmative.
Runtime inverts the LLM verdict post-call.
The LLM NEVER sees a negated question.

— Negation parser rule (§3.1.1) —
Matrix-predicate negation REJECTED in
predicate slot (lexicon: not, never,
fails to, lacks, excludes, omits, forbids,
prohibits, prevents, denies, devoid of, …).
Constituent negation inside noun phrases
('a function with no required arguments')
is LEGAL in subject/object slots.

— Quantifier (NEW v9) —
quantifier: at-least-one (default) | each |
exactly-one | at-most-one | none |
at-least-N | at-most-N · with optional scope:.

PreToolUse gate — 10 mechanical checks
(no LLM · no semantic analysis)

  1. Decorator present on every exported decl
  2. Every intent path resolves
  3. Every aspect/clause id resolves to a triple
  4. One intent per line
  5. @intent-ignore has both because=(...)
      and reason="..."
  6. Every statement inside a decorated   (v9)
      declaration is decorated
  7. @intent-support has a valid           (v9)
      3-slot triple
  8. No statement carries both @intent     (v9)
      and @intent-support for the same intent
  9. @intent-test/-test-file path ends in  (v9)
      any configured test_pyramid.suffix
 10. No matrix-predicate negation in     (round-3)
      @intent-support's predicate slot —
      author must use polarity: negative instead

Decorate-or-decompose (S ⊆ D) is NOT in the
gate (agentic). REPROMOTED to Sprint 9 as
/dusk-doctor --static-analysis for drift
detection — runs off the write path.

— dusk init merge strategy (round-3) —
Writes hook with _dusk_marker: 'dusk-pre-tool-
use-gate' + _dusk_managed: 'v1' as idempotency
anchor. On conflict with existing non-Dusk
PreToolUse entry matching Write/Edit: prompts
user [1] append (recommended), [2] replace
(writes .claude/settings.json.bak), [3] abort.
Never silent clobber. dusk doctor --check-hook
[--repair] verifies installation.

Gate is HARD: failed check → write rejected →
Engineer re-drafts. No 'warning' mode.

Decoration-completeness mandate (DESIGN)

Every line, call, assignment, statement,
expression, and lambda body — and their
contents — must be covered by intent
decorators appropriate to their participation.

When a code unit's contents include
operations whose intent participation
differs from the unit's decoration, the
unit is DECOMPOSED so each sub-operation
can be decorated appropriately.

v1 enforcement (round-3):
  · Engineer proactively applies the mandate
    (role prompt + decoration-completeness skill)
  · Verifier surfaces unsatisfied aspects when
    sub-operations participate in undeclared intents
  · /dusk-doctor --static-analysis (REPROMOTED to v1, Sprint 9)
    runs S⊆D call-graph check off the write path — drift detection,
    not real-time enforcement. Conservative default; --strict-unknowns
    surfaces undecorated callees.
  · NOT in the PreToolUse gate (agentic)

Examples
  pubsub.publish(syncChannel("n"), event)
    → channel-resolution intent ≠ publish
      intent → EXTRACT syncChannel call

  db.insert(x).values(y).returning()
    → all steps share intent footprint
      → keep as one statement

Language-agnostic: the rule speaks about
intent participation, not syntactic shape.
TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, SQL — same
rule.

Sub-agent roles (9) · memory · tool scope (advisory in v1)

1. Root Orchestrator   session   spawn + builds session-snapshot index
2. Bead Orchestrator   bead      spawn + commit + diagnosis routing + livelock
3. Decomposer          none      Read-only · typed relates_to (5 kinds)
4. Scout               none      Read + grep + AST
5. Engineer            bead      Write/Edit (gated) + Read + scoped Bash
6. Verifier            none      Read-only · fresh per call · polarity-aware
7. Test Runner         bead      Read + Bash(test-runner-cmd)
8. Author              dialog    Authoring + Read · polarity-decision skill
9. Conflict Resolver   none      Git ops + R/W · decorator-aware merge

Engineer ⊥ Verifier asymmetry — PROTECTED (round-3):
  Engineer persistent per bead → accumulates context via
      structured DUAL-CHANNEL bead memory (impl + test-authoring)
  Verifier fresh per call → spawn payload IDENTICAL across iters
      Diagnosis goes to Bead Orchestrator ONLY (never Verifier)
  Validated by fresh-Verifier audit (3 axes incl. citation precision)

Key skills (round-3):
  verifier · polarity-aware-evaluation
           · implies-evaluation (deterministic antecedents)
           · quantifier-checking · test-body-evaluation
  engineer · convergence-diagnosis · test-approach-taxonomy
  author   · polarity-decision · typed-relates-to
           · implies-antecedent-grammar
  orch.    · livelock-escalation-routing

Tool/skill scoping ADVISORY in v1 — PreToolUse gate provides
the actual safety boundary (hard sandbox deferred to v1.x).
Sub-agents spawn via Claude Code Task tool with subagent_type:
dusk-<role>; Dusk materializes memory + injects skills BEFORE
the spawn call.

Sub-agent memory scopes (v9 · round-3 hardened)

memory: none — Fresh per invocation. Spawn payload IDENTICAL
   across iterations (no diagnosis leak). Used by: Verifier,
   Decomposer, Scout, Conflict Resolver.

memory: bead — Persists across short-cycle iters + long-cycle
   samples + test-execution feedback. Used by: Engineer,
   Test Runner, Bead Orchestrator. STRUCTURED DUAL-CHANNEL format:
     - Current diagnosis (Bead-Orchestrator-scoped routing signal)
     - Approaches tried (impl)
     - Approaches tried (test-authoring) with Triple-slot focus tag
     - Verifier signals (last 3 verdicts)
     - Intent set in scope · Files being modified
   Mechanical/templated compaction — NEVER LLM-summarized.
   File at .ia/runtime/beads/<bead-id>/<role>.md.

memory: dialog — Author's 5-stage flow.
   .ia/runtime/dialogs/<dialog-id>/. 24h GC TTL.

memory: session — Root Orchestrator.
   .ia/runtime/session/<role>.md.

Implement checkpoint (round-3 — NOT a memory scope):
   .ia/runtime/implement/<resume_token>.json. 24h TTL. Survives
   harness crashes. Drives dusk_implement pause/resume contract.

Sub-agent spawn mechanism:
   Claude Code Task tool with subagent_type: dusk-<role>. Dusk
   materializes memory + injects skills BEFORE the spawn call.

Integration surface — MCP + slash (round-3)

MCP tools (mutating + flow):
  dusk_implement({request? | resume_token?})   pipeline OR resume
  dusk_author_start({request})         → dialog_id + first question
  dusk_author_continue({dialog_id, response})  loop until finalized
  dusk_author_finalize({dialog_id})    → intents_created
  dusk_resolve_livelock({bead_id, verb})  accept_test_as_is
                                          | modify_triple | escalate
  dusk_cancel({bead_id?, reason})  → CancelResult (cooperative)
  dusk_verify({diff, intents?})    → Verdict (ad-hoc)

Read-only fallback tools (paired with MCP resources):
  dusk_list_intents / dusk_get_intent
  dusk_list_traces / dusk_list_beads / dusk_get_bead
  dusk_list_implement_checkpoints · dusk_status · dusk_inspect

MCP resources (preferred when host browses):
  dusk://intents · dusk://intents/<path> · dusk://traces/recent
  dusk://beads/active · dusk://beads/<id> · dusk://implement-checkpoints

Slash commands (user-facing):
  /dusk-init · /dusk-author · /dusk-status · /dusk-verify
  /dusk-test · /dusk-benchmark · /dusk-doctor
  /dusk-doctor --static-analysis (S⊆D drift detection)
  /dusk-doctor --check-hook [--repair]

Harness contract — 4 capabilities (round-3, reduced from 5):
  spawn-by-type (Task tool) · PreToolUse hook (per-session)
  MCP host · filesystem trace emission
  (Skill scoping is Dusk-owned, not harness-provided.)

Every MCP tool returns success OR DuskError {kind, recoverable,
recovery_hint, …}. Pause/resume + cancellation are FIRST-CLASS
semantics, not afterthoughts.

Test pyramid encoding (v9 · round-3)

Reserved child-intent suffixes (CONFIGURABLE via
dusk.config.yml > test_pyramid.suffixes — defaults below):
  <impl-intent>/unit-tests          pure · no DB · no network
  <impl-intent>/integration-tests   cross-component · real DB
  <impl-intent>/e2e-tests           full journey · real HTTP + DB
  (extensible: contract-tests, property-tests, fuzz-tests, …)

Test intent triples (affirmative + polarity per round-3):
  covers-X        'the suite include a passing case verifying …'
  isolated-from-Y polarity: negative on 'depends on Y'
  count-bounds    quantifier: exactly-one + scope: per inserted row

Two-stage satisfaction (NEW v9 — round-3):
  1. Verifier evaluates the test BODY against the test-intent
     triples (does the test body actually verify what the triple
     claims?). A trivially-passing test FAILS this check.
  2. Test Runner executes only Verifier-validated tests.

Livelock detection (round-3):
  Same triple ≥3 iters + slot-focus ≥80% concentration +
  ≥3 structural test approaches (mock-call-order, time-spy,
  state-observation, snapshot-of-events, instrumented-mock, …)
  → TestVerifierLivelockReport → user resolves via
  dusk_resolve_livelock(accept_test_as_is | modify_triple |
  escalate).

Hierarchical satisfaction: parent X satisfied iff
  (X's triples pass via two-verdict {focal+support}) AND
  (every test-child satisfies BOTH stages).

Observability — trace event schema (v9 · round-3)

type SubAgentTrace = {
  schema_version: 1,                    (v9)
  trace_id, bead_id?, parent_trace_id?,
  role: '…' (9 roles incl. test-runner),
  invocation_site: '…' (incl. test-execution),
  model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens,
  latency_ms, cost_usd,
  input_summary?, output_summary?,

  confirmation_pass_outcome?:
     'confirmed_reject' | 'flaky_verdict_dismissed',

  // Stuck-bead debugging (round-3, short-cycle only)
  iteration_number?,
  verdict_delta_from_prior?,
  failing_triple_set?,
  engineer_change_summary?,

  stuckness_detector_state?,

    {failing_triple, slot_focus, structural_approach_count},

  skills_loaded?
}

Traces → .ia/observability/traces.jsonl
Verifier traces NEVER carry diagnosis fields
(diagnosis lives in Bead Orchestrator scope only).

What's new in v9 round-3 (key hardenings)

Constraint language
  · Polarity field replaces affirmative-only-by-rewriting.
    Slots stay affirmative; runtime inverts post-LLM.
    LLM NEVER sees negation. Matrix/constituent parser rule.
  · compose: implies with CLOSED antecedent vocabulary
    (is decorated with · claims any aspect of · is enclosed by
    a decoration of). Antecedents evaluated by deterministic
    INDEX LOOKUP, never LLM-judged.
  · quantifier vocab on triples + optional scope:.
  · Typed relates_to (5 kinds: parent · implies · conflicts ·
    supersedes · sibling). refines collapsed into parent.
  · Schema version 2 · automatic v8 migration.

Pipeline & runtime
  · Session-snapshot index (immutable for run) + per-bead
    in-memory delta. Reads carry index_snapshot_id.
  · Stuckness detector early-fires diagnosis; iter-5 fallback.
  · Diagnosis to BEAD ORCHESTRATOR only — Verifier spawn
    payload is identical across iterations (asymmetry protected).
  · 40-iter bead lifetime budget + 4-level recovery ladder
    (partial commit → intent-modification proposal → freeze → abort).
  · Long cycle: N=10 + N=2 confirmation pass on first reject
    (filters Verifier variance).
  · File-overlap + cross-bead focal/support overlap in DAG.

Verification
  · Per-triple verdict split: focal_verdict + support_quality.
  · Per-support-claim verdict (matches | mismatch | vague).
  · Fresh-Verifier audit: 3 axes (variance + similarity +
    CITATION PRECISION). No LLM-judge in the audit itself.
  · Two-stage test satisfaction: Verifier validates test body
    BEFORE Test Runner executes.
  · TestVerifierLivelockReport + dusk_resolve_livelock.

Integration surface
  · Harness contract: 4 capabilities (was 5). Tool/skill scoping
    is ADVISORY in v1; PreToolUse gate provides safety.
  · Sub-agent spawn via Claude Code Task tool.
  · dusk_implement pause/resume via disk checkpoint + resume_token
    (DuskError{kind: implement_paused_for_authoring}).
  · dusk_author_* continuation pattern (start/continue/finalize).
  · dusk_cancel: cooperative — drains in-flight Task calls,
    ordered cleanup, distinguishes cancelled[] from preserved[].
  · dusk_resolve_livelock + paired list/get tools + MCP resources.
  · DuskError envelope on every MCP tool.
  · dusk init writes hook with _dusk_marker idempotency anchor +
    conflict-prompting three-option merge. Never silent clobber.

Reading the example

The function declaration claims FIVE intents:
  notifications/send (primary, with aspects)
  db/use-drizzle-orm (cross-cutting · touched)
  sync/pubsub-on-create (cross-cutting · touched)
  observability/structured-logging (cross-cutting)
  error-handling/observable-failures (cross-cutting)

Inside the body, every statement is decorated:
  @intent          when the statement IS the focal
                       achievement of an aspect
  @intent-support  when the statement contributes
                       (with NL triple describing role)

Key structural moves (Engineer's discipline):
  · syncChannel("notification") extracted ABOVE the loop
      (loop-invariant hoist · check 8)
  · the event object extracted from the publish call args
      (no nested user fn call · check 8)
  · inArray(...) predicates extracted before Drizzle chains
  · Date.now() extracted to a named const
  · getLogger() extracted; payload object extracted;
      then logger.info(payload, msg)
  · let sent/skipped/failed collapsed to one counters obj
  · else-if chain flattened with continue

Verifier reads SCOPED — per aspect, not whole function:
  for publish-sync-per-insert it reads ~4 lines
  (focal + 3 support claims), not the 90-line body.

elements.text: Closing — v9 round-3 hardens the model into measurable properties. Polarity moves negation outside the LLM call. compose: implies makes conditional rules deductive (antecedents are facts, consequents are judgments). The session snapshot makes parallel reads deterministic. The recovery ladder converts thrashing into productive partial commits. The N=2 confirmation pass filters Verifier variance from regression detection. Three-axis fresh-Verifier audit makes the Engineer ⊥ Verifier asymmetry falsifiable. The diagnosis routes to the Bead Orchestrator only — the Verifier remains genuinely fresh. Build for right. Land the plane.
